learning_objective: 🎯 Discover how the world shifted from hand-made goods to massive machine-powered factories, and how this revolution drastically changed the lives of weavers and workers in Britain and India.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Even before factories dotted the landscape, there was large-scale industrial production for an international market. This was 'Proto-industrialisation', where merchants supplied money to peasants and artisans in villages to produce goods by hand.

In Victorian Britain, human labor was cheap and plentiful. Industrialists actually preferred hand labor over expensive, unreliable steam machines, especially for products that required intricate, varied designs which machines couldn't produce.

India was famous for fine cotton and silk. When the British East India Company gained power, they appointed paid servants called 'Gomasthas' to strictly supervise weavers. Later, British machine-made cloth flooded India, ruining the traditional weavers.

Despite colonial hurdles, Indian entrepreneurs (like Dwarkanath Tagore and J.N. Tata) set up cotton and jute mills in Bombay and Calcutta. To get workers, industrialists employed 'Jobbers'—old, trusted workers who brought people from their villages to the city.

fun_activity.title: 🖼️ Advertisement Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Search online for 'vintage Indian calendar advertisements' from the early 1900s. You will see British companies using images of Indian gods (like Krishna or Saraswati) to sell things like soap or baby food! It was a clever strategy to make foreign products feel familiar.

exam_tips: 📌 Why did Victorian industrialists prefer hand labor over machines? (Cheap labor, seasonal demand, machines were costly and broke down often, machines couldn't make intricate designs). This is a top 5-mark question.
📌 The role of the 'Gomastha': Know why traditional weavers clashed with these new, arrogant company servants who lacked village social links.
📌 Understand how the 'Swadeshi Movement' helped Indian industries grow by boycotting foreign goods and boosting domestic production.
quick_recap: ⭐ Industrialization started in villages (proto-industrialization) before moving to factories.
⭐ The introduction of machines like the Spinning Jenny caused fear and riots among traditional hand-spinners.
⭐ Colonial rule systematically destroyed India's handloom industry to benefit British factories, but Indian entrepreneurship eventually took root.
